NONE: › existing in fact, although perhaps not intended, legal, or accepted
事實上的，實際上的
› also defacto a person someone lives with as a wife or a husband, although they are not married
實質婚姻中的妻子（或丈夫）；同居伴侶

example: The city is rapidly becoming the de facto centre of the financial world.
這座城市正在迅速成為實質的金融中心。
He's her de facto husband though they're not actually married.
他們雖然沒有結婚，但他實際上是她的丈夫。
English is de facto the common language of much of the world today.
實際上，英語是當今世界大部分地區的常用語言。
If it is on British soil then it is de facto British.
如果它在英國的土地上，那麼它實際上就是屬於英國。
Compare
de jure
They've invited Joanne and her de facto for lunch on Sunday.
他們已經邀請喬安妮和她的伴侶星期天來吃午飯。

NONE: › If you look at someone or speak to someone de haut en bas, you do it in a way that shows you think you are superior to them. De haut en bas is French for "from high to low".
（法語）從上到下；態度傲慢地，居高臨下地

example: She looked at me de haut en bas and asked "And where do you come from?"
她傲慢地看著我，問道：「那麼你是哪裡人？」
He had a very de haut en bas approach to teaching.
他秉持一種居高臨下的教學方式。

NONE: › having a right or existence as stated by law
法律上（的）；根據法定權力（的）

example: The country has de facto independence now, and it will soon be recognized de jure by the world's governments.
該國事實上已經獨立，並將很快獲得世界各國政府的正式承認。
The president aims to create a de jure one-party state.
總統力圖建立一個合法的一黨制國家。
Compare
de facto adjective adverb

NONE: › used to say that someone is like a modern version of a person from the past. De nos jours is French for "of our days".
（法語）當代的

example: Justin Bieber - an Elvis Presley de nos jours
賈斯汀·比伯——當代的艾維斯·普雷斯利

NONE: › demanded by fashion, custom, etc.
（在時尚、習慣等方面）必需的，必備的，不可缺少的

example: Where I work, suits are de rigueur for all employees.
在我工作的地方，西裝是所有職員的必備之物。

NONE: › unnecessary, unwanted, or more than is suitable
不必要的；無用的；過頭的

example: I thought her remarks about Roger's recent problems were rather de trop.
我認為她對羅傑近來問題的評論說得有些過頭了。

NONE: › to (cause to) become less dangerous or difficult
（使）緩和，（使）緩解

example: The government has taken these measures in an attempt to de-escalate the conflict.
政府已採取這些措施試圖緩和衝突。
There are signs that the confrontation is beginning to de-escalate.
有跡象顯示對立已經開始緩和。

NONE: › to remove ice from something
給…除冰；給…除霜

example: to de-ice the car
給汽車除霜

NONE: › a substance for removing ice
除冰劑；除霜劑
› to get rid of feelings of stress (= worry caused by difficult situations in your life or job)
（使）放鬆

example: I began doing yoga as a way to de-stress.
我開始做瑜伽使自己放鬆。
Create a relaxing bedroom environment to de-stress you and help you fall asleep.
營造輕鬆的臥室環境可使自己放鬆，有助於睡眠。
